idea-plugin.name: OI Runner
idea-plugin.description:
Runs or debugs the C/C++ file you are looking at, using CLion's own single-file build, then prints wall time, CPU time and peak memory into the Run console when the process exits. The wall time comes from the kernel's own process timestamps, so it stays accurate for programs that redirect stdin/stdout with freopen and finish before the console appears, and debug sessions are timed on the debuggee itself instead of the whole debugger session. Release and debug builds get separate compiler options, editable under Settings | Tools | OI Runner.

The OI Cases tool window keeps a list of test cases for the file you are looking at: input, expected output and the actual output of the last run, one tab per case, with the lines that do not match painted red. The plugin compiles the file once and runs it once per case with a time limit and a memory limit, then writes the verdict on each tab and rolls the run up as "AC 3 · WA 1". Test cases can be imported from a folder of 1.in/1.out pairs or from a .zip of them, or simply by dragging that folder or archive onto the panel; cases are stored in the project's .idea directory, so a whole problem folder can be shared as-is.
